name: American Samoa
summary_text:
A US territory governed partly through chiefly custom (fa'a matai). Same-sex conduct is not criminalised in the modern code (decriminalised in the early 1980s; no audited source documents any enforcement since), but American Samoa was long the one US territory where federal marriage equality did not plainly apply — the attorney general said in 2015 it was 'still being reviewed' while every other territory adopted it, and the local constitution defines marriage traditionally. As US nationals, residents and visitors carry the 2025–26 federal document and screening friction, with no local non-discrimination shield of substance.

The Pacific academic record documents fa'afafine — a long-standing third-gender presence in Samoan family life — while contemporaneous travel advice describes a traditional, church-centred society where custom sets conformity. For an outed trans visitor: no criminal law, minimal institutional protection, unresolved questions about which federal guarantees reach the islands, and communal rather than state pressure.

sources.claim_summary: Advocates for Trans Equality 'Know Your Rights' guide to US airport security (TSA): covers screening issues for trans travellers - body scanners flagging anatomy, pat-downs, documentation mismatches, and how to request alternative screening. Relevant to American Samoa as a US territory under US TSA procedures.

Human Rights Watch (Mar 2026): 'US State Revokes Gender-Affirming Identification' — Kansas voids birth certificates and driver's licenses not matching sex assigned at birth; relevant to US-territory document policy.

University of Hawaii library research guide on Pacific sexual identity: academic resource collection on gender diversity and sexual identities across the Pacific, including American Samoa (fa'afafine and related third-gender traditions).
Out Traveler 'Ask the Expert' (2009): reader question on whether American Samoa is gay-friendly for a honeymoon - travel-editor answer describing the Samoan archipelago and tolerance context.

The Independent (July 2015): American Samoa may be the only US territory where the Supreme Court's same-sex marriage ruling does not apply - the Attorney General said the territory was 'still reviewing' the decision; every other territory adopted it voluntarily.
